delegates.summary:
## Outcome: **pass** — no task limit is broken, with large margin. The robustness picture is mixed and I would call the clearance *statistically* fragile but *structurally* sound.

I reproduced the reported metrics from the artifacts (recomputed OOS sharpe 1.9335 vs reported 1.9336; max_dd 0.0117 exactly) and re-ran all sweeps myself on dev bars only. I did not touch `kapso_evaluation/private_dir.txt`, did not run `evaluate.py`, and read only `results/*.csv` for aggregate slicing. My scratch work is in `/tmp/riskrev/` (dev bars copied from `/home/ubuntu/fixture/examples/trading/campaign/kapso_datasets/bars`); nothing in the repo was modified.

### 1. Limits — all respected, nothing close to a breach

The task names exactly one limit: position in `[-1, 1]` per instrument per bar.

| | dev | OOS 2024 | limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| max abs position | 0.721 | **0.6351** (GAMMA) | 1.0 |
| mean gross exposure (Σ\|pos\|/3) | — | 0.196 (max 0.371, p95 0.311) | none set |
| max_drawdown | 1.88% | 1.17% | reported, not constrained |
| annual turnover | 8.5 | 8.4 | reported, not constrained |
| worst month | −1.74% | −0.87% | none set |

Max \|position\| uses 64% of the allowed envelope at its single worst bar; the evaluator exited 0. `max_drawdown` and `turnover` are reported-only per the brief, so there is no limit to break there. One note for the feedback writer: the 1.17% drawdown is not evidence of risk control — it is a scale artifact of `TARGET_VOL=0.12` at mean gross 0.196. Rescaled to mean gross 1.0 the same curve implies ~6.0% max_dd, ~13.4% annual vol, ~43x turnover. The brief says that rescaling is Sharpe-neutral, so this is a presentation point, not a finding.

One dead branch worth recording: `LEV_CAP=3.0` is inert. Dev results are byte-identical at `LEV_CAP` 1.0 and 10.0, because every instrument's annual vol (0.190/0.287/0.150) exceeds `TARGET_VOL=0.12`, so leverage is always < 1. It stayed inert in 2024 (OOS max \|pos\| 0.635 < dev 0.721 implies OOS vol was not lower). It is an untested tail path, but the final `.clip(-1,1)` bounds it, so it cannot break the contract.

### 2. Robustness — the edge is concentrated in H2 2024, and that is the real finding

| slice | n | sharpe | total ret | max_dd |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| full 2024 | 262 | **+1.93** | +5.40% | 1.17% |
| T1 (Jan–Apr) | 87 | −0.57 | −0.43% | 0.99% |
| T2 (May–Aug) | 87 | +2.46 | +2.72% | 1.05% |
| T3 (Sep–Dec) | 88 | +3.50 | +3.04% | 1.17% |
| H1 | 131 | **−0.28** | −0.36% | 0.99% |
| H2 | 131 | **+3.82** | +5.78% | 1.17% |

Jackknife — **removing the strongest sub-period**:
- drop Q4 (strongest quarter) → **1.25**; drop Q3 → **1.30**. Both still clear 1.0, barely.
- drop T3 (strongest third) → **1.22**; drop T2 → 1.61.
- drop *both* strong quarters (Q1+Q2 only, 130 days) → **−0.19**. H1 alone → −0.28.

So: the clearance survives removal of any single quarter or third, but the entire year's edge lives in the second half. Equity was below its 1.0 starting value until **2024-07-10** — 6.3 months of the scored year was cumulatively flat-to-negative — 89% of days were underwater, longest underwater run 108 trading days, 5 of 12 months negative, losing-day fraction 45.8%.

Statistical margin, which is the sharper concern than the slicing:
- Sharpe SE at 262 days ≈ **0.984** (Lo). 95% CI **[0.00, 3.86]**; z against the 1.0 target = **+0.95**, one-sided p = **0.17**.
- Block bootstrap (block 10d, 20k resamples): median +1.93, 5–95% [+0.28, +3.61], **P(SR ≤ 1.0) = 17.6%**, P(SR ≤ 0) = 2.9%.

The attempt's own `eval_profile.md` pre-registered this noise floor ("SE ≈ 1.0 at ~250 bars... dev worst-year is the floor, not the central estimate") — and dev worst year is **2023 = 0.91**, i.e. *below* the target. By the attempt's own declared standard the honest floor sits under 1.0. That is the cleanest statement of the fragility.

Is the concentration anomalous for this design, or normal? I built the matched-length comparison (391 overlapping 262-day dev windows):
- day-level concentration is **normal**: OOS top-10 days = 79% of summed return, which is the 74th pct of dev windows (dev median 64%). OOS sharpe excluding the best 10 days = +0.48, the 29th pct; **52% of matched dev windows also fall below 1.0 under that test**. So "it dies without its best 10 days" is a property of a daily trend strategy at this Sharpe, not a defect of this year. Do not over-weight it.
- the **within-year regime split is at the tail**: the H1−H2 gap of −4.10 exceeds 95% of matched dev windows (dev p95 |gap| 3.73, max 4.95). OOS H1 (−0.28) is the 4th pct of dev half-year windows; OOS Q1 (−0.45) the 6th pct of dev quarter windows (dev worst half-year −0.97, worst quarter −1.76). 2024H1 was a bad-but-not-unprecedented regime; 2024 as a whole is a tail draw on the *sequencing*, not on the level.

Dev's own trajectory already showed decay: per-year 2021H2 **+2.92**, 2022 **+3.01**, 2023 **+0.91**, then 2024 +1.93 (H1 negative). 2 of 10 dev quarters were negative. Volatility is stable across windows (dev 2.71% vs OOS 2.63%), so the degradation is in the signal's mean, not in sizing.

### 3. Parameter neighbourhood — **confirmed flat**, but three of the four axes the notes cite are flat for mechanical reasons

I re-ran every sweep on dev (2021-07-01..2023-12-29) myself. The plateau is real:

- **Weight simplex**, 66 grid points at step 0.1 summing to 1: dev sharpe min **1.983**, median 2.167, max 2.256. **100% of the grid clears 1.5**; 98% clears 2.0. The chosen (0.45, 0.20, 0.35) scores 2.182 = the **62nd percentile**, *not* the dev argmax (2.256 at 0.0/0.3/0.7). No weight tuning to the peak.
- **BRK_W × CLS_W** (the two parameters that actually move the metric), 7×7 = 49 cells: a smooth single hill, min **1.52** at the far corner, max 2.19 near the chosen point. Every cell clears 1.5. BRK_W=20 is the row-wise argmax, but ±100% on it costs only ~0.15–0.2 sharpe (BRK_W 10 → 1.99, 40 → 2.04).
- **Component ablation**: trend-only 1.98, breakout-only 2.14, close_strength-only 2.12, and every pairwise blend 2.12–2.23. No single component carries the result; the ensemble is not propping up a dead leg. Notably `close_strength` (the only intrabar feature, w=0.35) is not load-bearing — dropping it entirely (0.7/0.3/0) still gives 2.095.
- **TREND_PAIRS**: single pairs (4,16) 2.17 and (8,32) 2.17, (2,8) 1.96, (16,64) 1.92, (32,128) 1.60. The chosen two-pair blend 2.182 is not better than its members — again no peak-picking.

Caveat on the claim as written: **TARGET_VOL and LEV_CAP flatness is not evidence of anything.** TARGET_VOL is 2.182 constant across 0.04→0.15 — that is the brief's own "uniform leverage is Sharpe-neutral" arithmetic, nothing more (it only moves dd: 0.63%→2.35%). LEV_CAP is exactly inert (identical at 1.0 and 10.0). `VOL_W` (2.182→2.218 across 20–250) and `FC_VOL_SPAN` (2.182→2.191 across 10–120) are nearly flat too — which means the vol-targeting machinery contributes essentially nothing to the Sharpe and functions only as a drawdown dial. The notes' plateau claim is **true**, but the load-bearing evidence is the weights/BRK_W/CLS_W/TREND_PAIRS surfaces I swept, not the four axes cited.

### 4. Cost assumption — **not load-bearing**; `cost_stress.txt` is honest

I reproduced `cost_stress.txt` exactly from an independent driver (5bp → 2.182, 10bp → 2.025, 20bp → 1.712, 40bp → 1.086) and extended it:

```
 0bp (0x) -> 2.338    15bp (3x) -> 1.868    50bp (10x) -> 0.774
 5bp (1x) -> 2.182    20bp (4x) -> 1.712    80bp (16x) -> -0.161
10bp (2x) -> 2.025    30bp (6x) -> 1.399
```

The 5bp charge costs 0.156 of 2.338 gross dev Sharpe — **6.7% of the gross edge**. Degradation is linear at ~0.157 sharpe per 5bp; dev crosses 1.0 at roughly **42bp (8.4x)** and zero at ~75bp (15x). Turnover is invariant at 8.5 across all cost rates (the signal does not react to the rate), so the stress is a clean re-pricing.

Turnover is internally consistent with the model. 8.4x/yr per instrument = mean daily \|Δpos\| of 0.033, i.e. a ~30-trading-day holding period, which matches the (4,16)/(8,32) EWMAC and 20-day feature horizons. Max single-day turnover is 0.136/0.109/0.150 — smooth repositioning, no flip-flopping that a per-unit cost model would under-charge. Dev 8.5 → OOS 8.4 means the cost charge was predictable out of sample. Cost drag is 0.42% of unit notional/yr against a 5.61% gross annual return (7.5% of gross P&L). The evaluator's implied same-bar-close fill is more favourable than a next-open fill, but a 30-day-horizon design is the least exposed kind to that gap.

### 5. Verdict for the feedback writer

This is a **clean, well-governed clearance of the 1.0 target with ample margin on the only limit the task actually names, but a statistically thin margin on the metric itself**. Max \|position\| 0.6351 against a 1.0 cap, max_dd 1.17%, turnover 8.4 — nothing is near a breach, and the parameter neighbourhood is genuinely flat (every one of 66 weight-simplex points and all 49 BRK_W×CLS_W cells clear 1.5 on dev; the chosen point is the 62nd percentile, not the argmax), so this is not a tuned spike and the 5bp cost assumption is not load-bearing (survives 8x). What is fragile is the *evidence*, not the construction: 1.93 at 262 days carries SE ≈ 0.98, so the target is cleared by 0.95 standard errors (bootstrap P(SR ≤ 1.0) = 17.6%), the whole year's P&L arrives after 2024-07-10 (H1 −0.28 / H2 +3.82, a split at the 95th percentile of matched dev windows), and dev's own worst year — the floor the attempt itself pre-registered as the honest estimate — is 0.91, below target. What I would watch: (a) the per-year decay 2.92 → 3.01 → 0.91 → 1.93-with-negative-H1, which suggests the signal's mean, not its sizing, is eroding; (b) whether anything in experiment 2 is chosen using the 2024 quarterly numbers now sitting in `output_data_generic_exp_0/risk_line.txt` — the attempt correctly flagged this itself and left experiment 2 unspent, and the pre-registered fallback in `PLAN.md` (trend alone, no vol targeting) is the only legitimate source; (c) the vol-targeting block, which earns no Sharpe (flat across VOL_W 20–250) and is purely a drawdown dial — if a future attempt wants Sharpe it must come from the forecast, not the sizing. One small documentation defect: `changes.log` says H1's losses were "the choppy, range-bound regime the design was pre-registered as losing in", but neither `PLAN.md` nor `eval_profile.md` contains any such pre-registration — the regime attribution is post-hoc and should be stated as such. Recommended exploration axis for the next attempt: **signal horizon / forecast diversification**, aimed at reducing the H1/H2 sequencing dependence rather than raising the headline — evidence being that the headline's SE is ~0.98 so any gain under ~0.3 is unmeasurable, while a sub-period Sharpe floor above 0 is a real improvement.

## Axis frontier

1. **Input representation — moved, near-saturated by construction.** Added intrabar close-location from high/low (dev IC +0.058/+0.074/+0.108). Measured dead and excluded: volume vs |next-day return| ≤ +0.062; bar range ≤ |0.079| and wrong-signed; `open − prev close` is identically zero in this snapshot. Cross-sectional features are **structurally unavailable** — the evaluator calls `signal` once per instrument; a genuine saturation, not a tenure claim. Headroom: component pnl correlations 0.80–0.92 say diversification is real but modest, and the ablation shows close_strength is **not** load-bearing (dropping it entirely still gives 2.095) — the intrabar channel is cheap, not decisive. *Untried:* (a) a range-based vol estimator (Parkinson / Garman-Klass from high/low) replacing close-to-close EWMA σ in both the forecast normaliser and the risk target; (b) signed-range asymmetry, (high−close) vs (close−low) over a trailing window, as a distinct estimator.
2. **Training distribution — untouched, NOT saturated, the axis with the least evidence against it.** Nothing was fitted; the design is a fixed prior. The only evidence is the rejected expanding ridge (dev 0.34–0.45, 2023 negative) at ~250 obs/instrument. That is a recorded strong prior with an explicit reopening condition, not a closed door: *the failure cause was sample size, so pooling all three instruments into one training set (3× obs; cross-instrument return correlation ≈ 0, so near-independent) with heavy shrinkage toward the ensemble prior addresses the recorded cause and may be tried.* *Also untried:* sample weighting by trailing forecast dispersion; purged/embargoed walk-forward example construction.
3. **Model mechanism — moved most, partly saturated with measurement.** Ensemble of 3 estimators × 2 speeds, tanh-squashed. Speed surface measured: (2,8) 1.96, (4,16) 2.17, (8,32) 2.17, (16,64) 1.92, (32,128) 1.60, (64,256) −0.74 — a broad hill; the baseline's 20/100 sits in the dead band. Weight simplex flat across all 66 points. *Untried:* regime-conditional speed weighting by a trailing vol or autocorrelation ratio (the H1/H2 split is exactly the symptom this targets); a fourth estimator from a different statistic family (e.g. trailing rank of cumulative return) rather than a fourth speed.
4. **Decoding / post-processing — saturated, with a correction to the attempt's own claim.** The notes cite TARGET_VOL (0.10–0.18 → 2.18 flat), VOL_W (2.182→2.218 over 20–250) and FC_VOL_SPAN (2.182→2.191 over 10–120) as plateau evidence. That flatness is **mechanical, not evidential** — the brief's own arithmetic makes uniform leverage Sharpe-neutral, so TARGET_VOL is a drawdown dial (0.63%→2.35% dd across the sweep) and the vol-targeting block **earns no Sharpe at all**. `LEV_CAP=3.0` is provably **inert**: dev results are byte-identical at LEV_CAP 1.0 and 10.0, because every instrument's annual vol (0.190/0.287/0.150) exceeds TARGET_VOL=0.12, so leverage never exceeds 1 — an untested tail path, safely bounded by the final clip. The real plateau evidence is the weights/BRK_W/CLS_W/TREND_PAIRS surfaces. No-trade band measured and rejected (0.03: turnover 9.5→8.6, ~0 Sharpe; 0.10: −0.12). *If a future attempt wants Sharpe, it must come from the forecast, not the sizing.*
5. **Validation protocol — moved, with the clearest remaining headroom.** Dev split 2021H2–2023 with 6-month warm-up, per-year reporting, 2/4/8× cost stress, frame-length invariance and single-bar perturbation causality probes. But selection was made on one dev window with per-year Sharpes as a crude stability proxy — **no rolling-origin folds and no bootstrap CI were run inside the session**; both were supplied after the fact. *Untried:* (a) rolling-origin re-selection — choose weights on 2021–2022 and score 2023, then invert, to price the selection cost directly rather than infer it; (b) a matched-length-window distribution of the dev Sharpe as the pre-registered expectation band, so an OOS draw is judged against a distribution instead of a point.
